subject: Reasoning
topic: Logical Venn Diagrams — Classification and Set Membership (W11 B1)

questions.stem: Which Venn diagram best represents the relationship between: Dogs, Animals, Mammals?

options.option_text: Three separate non-overlapping circles
Three concentric circles (Dogs inside Mammals inside Animals)
Mammals and Dogs overlap; Animals is separate
All three circles partially overlap with each other

questions.explanation: B is correct. Dogs ⊂ Mammals ⊂ Animals. All dogs are mammals, all mammals are animals. So the correct representation is three concentric circles: Dogs (innermost) inside Mammals inside Animals (outermost). Trap: Partially overlapping would mean some dogs are not mammals or some animals are not dogs — but these are complete subset relationships.

questions.stem: Which Venn diagram best represents the relationship between: Males, Doctors, Females?

options.option_text: Males and Females overlap; Doctors is separate
Three separate non-overlapping circles
Males and Females are separate; Doctors overlaps with both Males and Females
Doctors is inside Males; Females is separate

questions.explanation: C is correct. Males and Females are disjoint (no one can be both). Doctors can be male OR female — so Doctors overlaps with Males (male doctors) and also overlaps with Females (female doctors). Trap: A incorrectly makes Males and Females overlap; B makes no connection between Doctors and males/females; D incorrectly places all doctors inside the Male circle (ignoring female doctors).

questions.stem: In a survey of 100 students: 60 play cricket, 45 play football, and 25 play both. How many play neither cricket nor football?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Using inclusion-exclusion: n(C ∪ F) = n(C) + n(F) − n(C ∩ F) = 60 + 45 − 25 = 80. Students playing at least one sport = 80. Students playing neither = 100 − 80 = 20. Trap: 25 = n(C ∩ F) — wrong, that's the number playing both; 15 = 100−85 (arithmetic error); 10 = 100−90 (wrong).

questions.stem: In a group of 70 people: 37 like coffee, 52 like tea, and some like both. If every person likes at least one of the two, how many like both?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Every person likes at least one → n(C ∪ T) = 70 (no one is excluded). n(C ∪ T) = n(C) + n(T) − n(C ∩ T). 70 = 37 + 52 − n(C ∩ T). n(C ∩ T) = 89 − 70 = 19. Trap: 15 = 52−37 (wrong — just the difference of the two sets); 17 and 21 = arithmetic errors.

questions.stem: Which Venn diagram best represents: Fruits, Mangoes, Yellow things?

options.option_text: Mangoes inside Fruits; Yellow things overlaps with both Mangoes and Fruits
Three concentric circles — Mangoes inside Fruits inside Yellow things
All three are completely separate
Mangoes inside Fruits; Yellow things is completely separate

questions.explanation: A is correct. All mangoes are fruits → Mangoes ⊂ Fruits. Not all fruits are yellow (apples, grapes, grapes are red/green). Not all yellow things are fruits (yellow cars, yellow flowers). Some fruits are yellow (bananas, mangoes) → Yellow things overlaps with Fruits. Some mangoes are yellow but not all (Alphonso mango is yellow, some mangoes are green). So: Mangoes entirely inside Fruits; Yellow things partially overlaps with Fruits (including some area where it also covers part of Mangoes). Trap: B makes all yellow things fruits — wrong (yellow cars); D makes Yellow things completely separate — wrong (yellow fruits exist).

questions.stem: In a class of 80 students: 45 study Maths, 50 study English, 25 study both. How many study only Maths?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Students studying ONLY Maths = Total Maths − Both = 45 − 25 = 20. Students studying ONLY English = 50 − 25 = 25. Students studying at least one = 20 + 25 + 25 = 70. Students studying neither = 80 − 70 = 10. Trap: 25 = students in both (not 'only maths'); 45 = total maths students including those in both; 30 = 45−15 (wrong subtraction).

questions.stem: Which Venn diagram best represents: Squares, Rectangles, Polygons?

options.option_text: Squares and Rectangles overlap; Polygons is separate
Three concentric circles — Squares inside Rectangles inside Polygons
Squares inside Polygons; Rectangles is separate
All three separate non-overlapping circles

questions.explanation: B is correct. All squares are rectangles (a square is a special rectangle with all sides equal) → Squares ⊂ Rectangles. All rectangles are polygons (4-sided closed figures) → Rectangles ⊂ Polygons. Therefore: Squares ⊂ Rectangles ⊂ Polygons, represented by three concentric circles (Squares innermost, Rectangles middle, Polygons outermost). Trap: Separate circles means squares are not rectangles — wrong by definition; overlapping circles means some squares are not rectangles — also wrong.

questions.stem: In a group of 200 people, 120 read newspaper A and 80 read newspaper B. If 40 read both, how many read at least one newspaper?
questions.explanation: C is correct. n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B) = 120 + 80 − 40 = 160. So 160 people read at least one newspaper. People reading neither = 200 − 160 = 40. Trap: 200 = total group (assumes everyone reads at least one — not stated); 120 = only reads A (excludes those reading only B and both).

questions.stem: Which Venn diagram best represents the relationship between: Pen, Pencil, Stationery?

options.option_text: Three concentric circles — Pen inside Pencil inside Stationery
Pen and Pencil are separate; both are inside Stationery
Pen and Pencil overlap; Stationery is outside both
All three completely overlap at the centre

questions.explanation: B is correct. Pen and Pencil are distinct items (neither is the other). Both are types of Stationery. So: two separate circles (Pen and Pencil) both contained within the larger Stationery circle. Trap: Concentric circles means Pen ⊂ Pencil, which is wrong (a pen is not a type of pencil); Pen and Pencil overlapping means some pens are pencils — wrong; Stationery outside means pens/pencils are not stationery — wrong.

questions.stem: In a survey of 90 people: 45 like tea, 30 like coffee, and 15 like both tea and coffee. How many like only coffee?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Those who like ONLY coffee = Total coffee drinkers − Both = 30 − 15 = 15. Similarly, only tea = 45 − 15 = 30. At least one = 30+15+15 = 60. Neither = 90−60 = 30. Trap: 30 = total coffee drinkers (includes 'both' — not 'only'); 20 = wrong arithmetic; 10 = possible confusion with 'neither' calculation partial.
